structurePlan.overview: Brick-built, display-scale minifigure inspired by the reference: a blonde-hooded hero in an all-white outfit holding a blue “lightsaber.” Build in stacked brick/plate layers (BrickHeadz-like proportions) so it’s sturdy and achievable with the available white/gray inventory and accent colors.

subassemblies.name: Display base (optional)
subassemblies.description: Small rectangular stand to stabilize the figure and set the stance; keep it dark bluish gray/black with a light bluish gray edge.
subassemblies.image_location: Bottom of model (not visible in reference; adds stability under the feet).

subassemblies.name: Feet + lower legs
subassemblies.description: Two blocky feet with short shins. Primary color white, with light bluish gray/ tan greeble options for the subtle boot/leg pattern seen in the reference. Connect feet to hips with simple stacked bricks/plates.
subassemblies.image_location: Bottom of image: both feet and lower legs.

subassemblies.name: Hips / belt block
subassemblies.description: A 1–2 brick-tall waist section in white with a contrasting belt stripe (reddish brown/dark red) wrapping the front; add a small centered “buckle/pouch” using dark red/ reddish brown small plates/tiles.
subassemblies.image_location: Mid-lower area: the brown belt across the waist.

subassemblies.name: Torso / jacket body
subassemblies.description: Main chest volume in white. Suggest the crossed robe folds using subtle plate offsets and a few dark accents (dark bluish gray or black lines) without over-detailing. Build as a rigid box that the arms pin into from the sides.
subassemblies.image_location: Center of image: white torso with robe seams.

subassemblies.name: Arms (2)
subassemblies.description: Two white arms posed forward to grip the saber. Use simple hinged/stepped shoulders (plates/brackets if available; otherwise plate-stacking) so the hands meet at the centerline. End each arm with a small “hand” block in tan/light nougat tones if you choose to suggest skin.
subassemblies.image_location: Right/center: both arms held forward around the hilt.

subassemblies.name: Hands + saber grip cradle
subassemblies.description: A compact central clamp/‘fist’ assembly that locks between the two arms and holds the hilt. Build the grip cradle first, then attach arms to it so the pose is consistent and strong.
subassemblies.image_location: Center-right: where both hands meet on the lightsaber handle.

subassemblies.name: Lightsaber hilt
subassemblies.description: Short metallic cylinder using light/dark bluish gray round/curved elements and small black accents (to suggest the emitter/grip rings). Keep it stout so it can be supported by the hand cradle.
subassemblies.image_location: Center-right: silver handle below the blue blade.

subassemblies.name: Lightsaber blade
subassemblies.description: Straight, slightly tapered look using Medium Azure/Blue plates/tiles/1xN elements in a thin vertical stack; add trans-clear pieces near the tip if you want a “glow” highlight. Attach firmly to the hilt with a simple stud-to-stud connection.

subassemblies.name: Neck + head block
subassemblies.description: A compact head module: tan/light nougat face area on the front, with a mostly cubic head shape. Use a 1-plate inset to suggest the face plane vs. hair frame.

subassemblies.name: Hair (blonde)
subassemblies.description: Layered ‘helmet’ of tan/yellow elements over the head block, stepped to suggest shaggy hair. Prioritize a rounded silhouette via plates/tiles and slopes/curves if available; keep it symmetrical with a slight forward overhang.
subassemblies.image_location: Top of image: blonde hair around the head.

notes: Target size: ~10–14 bricks tall (including hair), with chunky ‘BrickHeadz-like’ proportions for stability.
Color blocking: mostly White for outfit; ReddishBrown/DarkRed for the belt; Tan/Yellow mix for hair; Light/Dark Bluish Gray for saber hilt; MediumAzure/Blue for blade.
If you run short on tan/yellow for hair, blend in MediumNougat or BrightLightYellow for highlights.
Keep the arms’ connection simple (plate-stacked shoulders) and let the central ‘hand cradle’ carry the saber so the blade doesn’t wobble.
Leg pattern in the reference can be suggested with a few tan/light bluish gray tiles/plates on the front of the shins rather than complex shaping.
